reports.title: LX-23 widened to 15 m — volume, propellant, and Δv reconciled
reports.author: Claude
reports.body: The 8 m body could not hold the LX-23's own ascent propellant (held ~213 t against ~500 t needed). Solving backward for the width that closes the ascent gave ~14 m; Franco set it to 15 m for margin. At 15 m the D-section integrates to ~1,713 m3 gross, ~1,068 m3 tank, ~886 t methalox. The vehicle went from volume-starved to closing with an on-orbit reserve. L/W 3.0, glide profile intact.

reports.title: LX-23 booster: twin TX-24 replaced by three fleet-common TX-04
reports.author: Claude
reports.body: Computing from real TX-04 masses (779 t prop, 39 t dry each), three methalox TX-04s in asparagus deliver ~50 t to LEO. This makes the TX-04 the fleet's ONLY booster: EX=1, VX=2, LX=3 — one design to develop, certify, and mass-produce. The bespoke TX-24 heavy core is held in reserve only. Requires the TX-04 to be a methalox variant for crossfeed (see the open propellant conflict on the Pauldron).

reports.title: LX-23 dry mass 60 t, payload 50 t, per-stage Δv from real masses
reports.author: Claude
reports.body: A bottom-up parts build-up gave ~60 t dry (not the earlier 75 t scaling guess). At 50 t payload the stack closes: Stage 1 (3× TX-04) ~3,660 m/s, Stage 2 (LX-23) ~7,780 m/s, total ~11,440 m/s vs ~11,000 needed — ~440 m/s on-orbit reserve (~310 m/s working after deorbit). Refuelling at the node is optional, only to extend Δv or go beyond LEO; the LX-23 reaches orbit and does its work unaided.

reports.title: GX-04 Curiass promoted to its own vehicle; sized for the 5 t common job
reports.author: Claude
reports.body: The old EX-4 mini-blueprint lander numbers (dry 4.0 / wet 15.7 / 10 t / 3,800 m/s) never closed simultaneously. Reworked for the common job — deliver 5 t to the surface, return crew + ~0.5 t: dry ~4.4 t, ~17 t propellant, ~27 t wet at the node, 3,800 m/s round trip. Sized for the common job (not the 10 t max) to minimise tanker runs. Four corner thrusters + central OMS replace the single descent engine.

reports.title: EX-2 Gawain resized 10 t → 5 t to fit the Efficient class
reports.author: Claude
reports.body: The 31 t / 10 t EX-2 was heavier than a V-22, violating the EX small/light class and overlapping heavy-lift competitors (e.g. Archer's Halo). Shrunk to 5 t payload / ~17 t MTOW — lighter than a V-22, a proper light EX-class vehicle. The shared airframe with the 12 t EX-1 medic is more honest at 17 t than it was at 31 t.
